issues.legal_issue: A single-member waqf tribunal retains jurisdiction until the state constitutes and notifies a three-member tribunal, and civil courts do not acquire jurisdiction merely because the replacement tribunal has not yet been constituted.
material_facts: A trust filed a suit asserting that the disputed property was waqf property before a single-member tribunal after amendments to the governing law provided for a three-member tribunal.
The state had not issued a notification constituting a three-member tribunal.
The High Court held that the single-member tribunal lacked jurisdiction and that the civil court could hear the dispute until a three-member tribunal was constituted.
issues.conclusion: The single-member tribunal continued to have jurisdiction until a three-member tribunal was constituted by notification; the civil court did not acquire jurisdiction in the meantime. The High Court's contrary ruling was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 83(1) and 83(4) of the Waqf Act, 1995, as amended, the state must constitute tribunals and the amended composition is three members. Section 85 bars civil-court jurisdiction over matters assigned to the tribunal. The amendment expanded the tribunal's composition but did not extinguish the existing tribunal before its replacement could function. Implied repeal is not readily inferred; it requires irreconcilable inconsistency, and a later law that cannot yet be implemented does not displace the earlier arrangement so as to create a jurisdictional vacuum. The Court relied on Om Prakash Shukla v. Akhilesh Kumar Shukla, AIR 1986 SC 1043; Municipal Council, Palai v. T.J. Joseph, AIR 1963 SC 1561; and Harshad S. Mehta v. State of Maharashtra, (2001) 8 SCC 257. Section 6(e) of the General Clauses Act, 1897, was also relevant to the treatment of proceedings instituted before the amendment.

predicates.waqf_property_proceeding: A party brings a proceeding to determine a dispute or other matter relating to waqf or waqf property.
predicates.existing_single_member_tribunal: A single-member tribunal constituted under the existing framework is available to hear the proceeding.
predicates.replacement_three_member_tribunal_not_no: The state has not notified the constitution of the replacement three-member tribunal.

issues.definition: When a waqf-property proceeding is brought while an existing single-member tribunal is available and its three-member replacement has not been notified, the single-member tribunal retains exclusive jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: An interim injunction granted by a functioning single-member waqf tribunal remains in force when the challenge to its continuation is dismissed.
material_facts: The tribunal granted an ad-interim injunction in the waqf-property suit.
The High Court did not interfere with the injunction and directed that it continue for a period after its judgment.
An appeal challenged the High Court's decision to leave the injunction in force.
The Supreme Court dismissed that appeal and expressly held that the tribunal's interim order would continue.
issues.conclusion: The appeal challenging continuation of the interim order was dismissed, and the interim order passed by the tribunal was to continue.
issues.legal_principle: The Court's ruling on the injunction followed its conclusion that the single-member tribunal continued to have jurisdiction until a three-member tribunal was constituted. The High Court had also found no basis to interfere with the interim order in revision, observing that whether the properties were waqf properties involved a mixed question of law and fact requiring evidence. The Supreme Court did not determine the merits of the injunction; it expressly held that the interim order would continue.

predicates.waqf_property_proceeding: A party brings a proceeding to determine a dispute or other matter relating to waqf or waqf property.
predicates.tribunal_granted_interim_injunction: The tribunal grants an interim injunction in the proceeding.
predicates.high_court_left_injunction_in_force: The High Court leaves the tribunal's interim injunction in force.
predicates.appeal_challenges_injunction_continuatio: A party appeals the decision to leave the tribunal's interim injunction in force.

issues.definition: When a tribunal has granted an interim injunction in a waqf-property proceeding, the High Court has left it in force, and an appeal challenges that continuation, the injunction continues if the appeal is dismissed.

issues.legal_issue: A state must take steps to constitute and notify a three-member waqf tribunal when the governing law requires that composition.
material_facts: The amended law required tribunals to consist of three members.
The states had not issued notifications constituting three-member tribunals.
The Supreme Court directed the states to take steps to constitute the tribunals and issue notifications.
issues.conclusion: The states were directed to take immediate steps to constitute three-member tribunals and issue the necessary notifications.
issues.legal_principle: Section 83(4) of the Waqf Act, 1995, as amended, provides for a three-member tribunal and uses mandatory language requiring the state to constitute it by notification. The Court treated the states' failure to perform that duty as requiring a direction to comply.

predicates.waqf_tribunal_administration_case: A proceeding concerns the administration or constitution of tribunals assigned to determine waqf disputes.
predicates.governing_framework_requires_three_membe: The governing legal framework requires the tribunal to have three members.
predicates.state_has_not_constituted_replacement_tr: The state has not constituted and notified the required three-member tribunal.

issues.definition: When a tribunal-administration proceeding concerns a framework requiring three-member tribunals and the state has not constituted the required tribunal, the state must constitute and notify it.
